statement: In 6 of 42 books a toy or animal companion is drawn mirroring the protagonist's feeling while saying nothing in the text (a cat in The Lost Ball, a toy rhino in Dudu's Hat, a blue frog on every spread of Play with Me); in the other 36 there is no companion or it does not mirror.

scope.population: contemporary open-licence picture books: Book Dash (35), African Storybook (2), StoryWeaver: Pratham Books (5), Room to Read (1); 2014-2026

analyst_note:
2026-10-14: Best Friends and An Unexpected Adventure (wordless) reviewed for this claim. Neither new book has a silent mirroring companion (Best Friends' companion speaks; the wordless book has none).
2026-10-15: No new support from any source. Khumo (Book Dash) and Good Night, Monu (StoryWeaver) carry a teddy on most spreads but its face does not track the child's. 2026-10-20: The Red Umbrella's duck hides when the children hide but reads as a running find-it joke; not counted either way.
2026-10-28: +2 support, +7 counter. First non-Book Dash support: The Lost Ball (Room to Read) — a cat never mentioned in the text copies Jami's dismay and worry. Book Dash: Dudu's Hat's rhino supports; A Day Out's dog and Goldfish Genius's cat react but mostly to others, not counted as mirroring. Sources of the new works: Book Dash — A Day Out, Who Ate My Hat, Let's Go Looking, Dudu's Hat, Clever Pig, A House for Mouse, Goldfish Genius; StoryWeaver — Get Down, Rocky! (Pratham Books), The Lost Ball (Room to Read, translated from Bangla).
2026-11-13: +1 support (Play with Me: an unnamed frog hides, cries when Jabu is alone and leaps when he plays), +9 counter (dogs in Can We Eat a Rainbow? and Alex's Super Medicine and the cat in Sweet Dreams act or sleep but do not mirror). Sources of the new works: Book Dash — A Trip to the Tap (2023), Going Places (2025), AAAAAHHH!!!! Mmawe! (2024), Can We Eat a Rainbow? (2026), I Can Do It! (2026), Play with Me (2026), Banzi's Busy Bees (2025), Dance, Khuzwayo, Dance! (2023), Alex's Super Medicine (2022); StoryWeaver — Sweet Dreams (Pratham Books, year not shown).

magicpaper.current: catalog companions speak and act in text
magicpaper.suggested: Hypothesis: a companion can amplify feeling silently, through the picture; relevant to companion illustration briefs.
magicpaper.note: Companions as emotional amplifiers, not protagonists.
